video_caption: The video opens with military personnel in camouflage uniforms working on a gray F-35 fighter jet inside a hangar, with one mechanic on a ladder accessing a panel and another using a tool on the aircraft's undercarriage. Following shots show an F-35 flying in the sky, sometimes alongside older propeller planes, and a robotic vacuum cleaner moving across a carpet with overlaid text "the problems with AESA". A man with short dark hair and a beard, wearing a black t-shirt and black jacket, stands in a room with bookshelves, introducing a discussion about AESA radar technology. He references a previous video and a news article about Northrop producing the new AN/APG-85 AESA radar for F-35 jets, suggesting that AESA has made other radar types "obsolete" and "PESA/AESA hybrids barely adequate" for combat. He then transitions to showing a close-up of a Rafale jet's open nose cone revealing its radar, and briefly cuts to a cozy scene of feet by a fireplace before returning to emphasize that AESA technology "may not have reached its maturity yet." He states that he will highlight "some of the problems" and "drawbacks" and "don'ts" of AESA, with accompanying text "Drawback" and "Don't" appearing onscreen, while a smiling blonde woman is shown next to a large radar dish. The video concludes with an F-35 performing a vertical take-off from an aircraft carrier deck, demonstrating its unique capabilities.

The video segment displays a technical diagram on a light blue background with faint circuit board patterns. On the left, a blue rectangular box is labeled "Signal Generation & Processing." Five blue lines extend from this central box to five smaller blue rectangular boxes arranged vertically on the right, each labeled "T/R" (Transmitter/Receiver). To the right of each "T/R" box, a small black T-shaped antenna element is depicted. Initially, a single yellow semicircular wave emanates from each of these five antennas. Then, more yellow semicircular waves quickly appear, layering three per antenna, forming a solid, vertical yellow-gold bar on the far right, illustrating a phased array antenna emitting a signal.

In this video segment, a man with dark hair and a beard, wearing a black t-shirt with a partially visible graphic ("THE MAN MYTH THE LEGEND VINTAGE 1968 AGED PERFECTI... ORIGINAL PART...") and a black blazer, speaks directly to the camera. He stands in front of a wooden bookshelf filled with books, with a framed picture behind him. As he speaks, he gestures with his hands, initially pointing and making a small "pinching" motion. Text overlays appear on the right side of the screen: "Sensitivity", "Gain", and "S/N ratio". The scene then quickly cuts to an external close-up of a fighter jet's nose, showing its radar covered by a distinctive orange and black honeycomb pattern, with "Visual c/o Phazotron. Credit" displayed. The video cuts back to the man, who continues to speak, holding a black tablet in his left hand, and gesturing with his right hand in a sweeping motion as the text "Versatility" appears. He then makes a larger gesture as a speech bubble with the text "Radary?" (meaning "Radar-like?" in Polish) and an image of a small round radar device appears. More text overlays emerge: "Communication", "Jamming", and "Passive detection". The scene briefly transitions to a close-up of a finger dialing a number on an old, light-colored rotary phone, specifically dialing the number "2". Finally, it cuts back to the man, who makes a dismissive gesture with his right hand before gesturing forward, and then transitions to a detailed view of a modern fighter jet cockpit, featuring large digital displays showing maps and data, a joystick, and a throttle, with "Visual c/o G5ng33. CC BY-SA 4.0" displayed at the bottom.

The video segment opens with a man with dark hair and a beard, wearing a black blazer over a black t-shirt that reads "THE MAN MYTH THE LEGEND VINTAGE 1968" (English translation), standing in front of a wooden bookcase. He speaks directly to the camera, gesturing with his hands as the text "Multifunction Arrays" appears in white on the right side of the screen. The scene then transitions to an outdoor street performance where a man and a woman, both on unicycles, juggle white clubs in front of a white van with colorful graffiti and an audience seated on the ground. The video cuts back to the man in the blazer, who continues to speak and gesture, looking serious. A large, translucent white question mark then overlays the man. This transitions to a silhouette of a military jet taking off from a runway against a sunset sky, with a question mark still visible. The jet ascends rapidly, leaving a fiery exhaust trail, and the question mark disappears as the jet flies higher into the darkening sky. Finally, the video returns to the man in the blazer, who is still talking and gesturing, as a white vertical bar with the number "4" (representing a countdown or a point in a list) appears on the left side of the screen. Following this, the word "Complexity" appears in white on the right, and shortly after, the word "Cost" appears below it.

The video segment features a sequence of visuals, beginning with an automated manufacturing machine precisely placing small electronic components onto a green circuit board in a factory setting. A white vertical bar with the number "4" is visible in the bottom left corner throughout several scenes. This transitions to a medium shot of a man with dark hair and a beard, wearing a black blazer over a black t-shirt that reads "THE MAN THE MYTH THE LEGEND VINTAGE 1968 AGED TO PERFECTION (MOSTLY)", standing in front of bookshelves and gesturing with his hands as he speaks. Following this, a detailed close-up of a complex electronic circuit board, possibly inside a casing, displays various chips, including one marked "ALTERA ACEX". The man returns to the screen, still gesturing, and text overlays appear and change from "Gallium Arsenide" to "Gallium Nitride". This is succeeded by a white whiteboard animation showing a hand-drawn bar graph in red, depicting increasing values with an upward arrow, and the word "FEES" written below, indicating rising costs. Finally, the man reappears in the same setting, continuing to speak and gesture, holding a dark object in his left hand.

The video begins with a man in a black jacket and a black t-shirt (with text "THE MAN THE MYTH THE LEGEND VINTAGE 1968 AGED TO PERFECTION") speaking in a room with bookshelves and a world map on the wall, a white vertical bar with the number "3" visible in the bottom left corner of the screen throughout the video. A close-up shot of small electronic circuit board components is shown (0:02), with text "Visual c/o A. Farina, P. Holbourn, L. Timmonen - AESA radar - Pan-domain multi-function capabilities for future systems. Credit" at the bottom. The speaker reappears (0:03) before an animated exploded diagram of an "Airborne AESA Configuration" (0:06) appears, labeling its various parts like "Array face strips," "Cowl," "Planks," "Motherboard," "RF Manifolds," "Frame," "Power Supply," "Control & Timing Interface," and "RF Interface." The video then cuts to a woman fanning herself with a blue fan, looking hot (0:11), followed by an external view of a large, circular AESA radar array mounted on a stand (0:14). The speaker returns (0:16), then a man is seen getting sprayed in the face with water from a garden hose (0:19). The speaker explains (0:21) and an animated graphic of a fighter jet (likely an F-15) flying, with colorful lines representing radar emissions, is displayed (0:26). An inset in the bottom left shows radar components on a testing rig, with text "Visual c/o Raytheon - APG-82. Credit." The speaker returns (0:30), and text overlays appear, first "Cooling System" (0:32), then "Thermal Management" (0:35). The speaker continues (0:37) and an animation shows two fighter jets (F-15s) flying with blue radar beams connecting them (0:40). A close-up shot of three small, golden electronic components next to a 1 Euro cent coin is shown (0:43), with text "Visual c/o FBN/P. Immerx - Ferdinand-Braun-Institut, Leibniz-Institut. CC BY Sa 4.0." The speaker concludes this segment (0:48). The video transitions to a close-up of a cockpit control stick with red buttons (0:53). Finally, a clear blue sky shot from a refueling aircraft shows an F-35 fighter jet approaching and connecting to a refueling boom for aerial refueling (0:56), with "UTAH" and "ANG" visible in red on the small wings of the refueling probe.

The video opens with a man in a black jacket and a black t-shirt that reads "THE MAN, THE MYTH, THE LEGEND, VINTAGE 1968, AGED TO PERFECTION, ORIGINAL PARTS." He stands in a room with wooden bookshelves filled with books and a framed map on the wall, gesturing with his right hand as he speaks. Text overlays appear, first "Processing Power," and then a thought bubble with "Before..." next to a white puck-like object, followed by a "Subscribe" button that changes to "Subscribed" with a bell icon. The scene then transitions to an outdoor shot on what appears to be an aircraft carrier deck, where two individuals in red shirts and brown pants are pushing a large, missile-shaped object on a small wheeled cart. Another person in similar attire walks nearby, and large machinery with oversized wheels is visible in the background. The video then cuts back to the man from the beginning, still speaking and gesturing, now holding a black tablet in his left hand, against the same backdrop of bookshelves and map.

The video segment opens with a close-up of a round radar array, likely part of an F-35 fighter jet, in a hangar setting, with some maintenance equipment visible around it (00:00). A man, wearing a black t-shirt with "THE MAN THE MYTH THE LEGEND VINTAGE 1968 AGED PERFECTED" text and a black jacket, then appears in a room with bookshelves in the background, gesturing with his hands as he speaks (00:05). The scene transitions to an F-35 fighter jet on an aircraft carrier deck at dusk, with a crew member signaling its take-off, characterized by the jet lifting off the deck against a vibrant orange and purple sky (00:08). Back to the man, he now holds a black tablet and gestures while text "Processing Power" appears on the right side of the screen (00:15). A close-up shot of a blue circuit board with various electronic components (capacitors, integrated circuits, and colorful connectors) then fills the screen, with the camera panning across it (00:20). The man returns, continuing his explanation with expressive hand gestures (00:24), followed by a brief, grayscale shot of a fighter jet cockpit, which quickly transitions to a YouTube video interface where a cursor clicks the "Join" and "Subscribed" buttons (00:28). The man reappears, speaking animatedly (00:30), then a detailed wax figure of Albert Einstein is shown with scientific equations on a blackboard behind him (00:34). The man is back on screen, still gesturing and holding the tablet (00:35), before a speech bubble with the text "Let it gooo..." appears next to him, accompanied by a small, illuminated white circular device rotating below it (00:43). Two military personnel, one in camouflage and the other in a flight suit, are next seen inspecting a laptop near the landing gear of an F-35 jet in a hangar (00:44). The man returns to the screen (00:47), followed by a view inside an anechoic chamber, where a man in a dark shirt and face mask is operating equipment connected to a large, square-framed, circular radar array (00:51). The segment concludes with the first man speaking directly to the camera, making emphatic gestures (00:54). Throughout the video, a large white vertical bar with the number "2" at its base is present on the left side of the screen.

The video opens with a man in a black blazer and a black t-shirt with white text ("VINTAGE 1968 AGED PERFECTLY ORIGINAL PARTS") standing in front of a bookshelf, holding a tablet and gesturing as he speaks. The scene then cuts to a large grey F-15 Eagle fighter jet inside a hangar, surrounded by several military personnel in camouflage uniforms who are inspecting the aircraft. They are seen walking around the jet, looking at various parts, and seemingly engaging in pre-flight checks or maintenance. One shot focuses on the main landing gear as soldiers gather around it, and another shows two soldiers talking animatedly near the jet's fuselage, with a red "REMOVE BEFORE FLIGHT" tag visible. The video then cuts back to the man in the blazer, who continues to speak and gesture, as a red box with white text appears on the right side of the screen: "PATRONS DO IT BETTER" and below it, a smaller red button reads "BECOME A PATRON."

The video segment opens in a clean, industrial-looking facility, possibly a factory, showing a row of several large, circular, metallic radar dishes, each with a textured, honeycomb-like surface, mounted on blue and white mobile stands. In the background, a picture of a fighter jet (likely an F-35 given the partially visible "APG-81" text) is displayed on a wall. The scene then transitions to a man with dark hair and a beard, wearing a black t-shirt with white text and a black blazer, standing in what appears to be an office or study. He gestures with his hands, explaining concepts, while behind him are wooden bookshelves filled with books and a framed map or artwork on the wall. Text overlays appear next to him, stating "Not fast enough" (indicating a potential limitation) and later "With the increase of frequency..." (suggesting a discussion about technical specifications). A large white number "2" remains visible in the bottom-left corner throughout the segment.

The video segment opens with an aerial shot of a large, white military aircraft, possibly a surveillance plane or tanker, as seen from another aircraft, suggesting an in-flight operation like refueling or close formation. The landscape below is a light, hazy terrain, possibly a desert. The scene then transitions to a medium shot of a man speaking to the camera. He has dark hair and a beard, and he is wearing a black t-shirt with a white graphic print and a black blazer. He holds a black tablet in his left hand and gestures with his right as he speaks. The background behind him features a wooden bookshelf filled with books, and a framed map or artwork hangs on the wall. Throughout the entire segment, the text "1 2" is visible in the bottom left corner of the screen.

The video opens with a man, wearing a black jacket over a black T-shirt with the text "THE MAN THE LEGEND VINTAGE 1968 AGED TO PERFECTION," speaking and gesturing while holding a tablet in his left hand. Behind him, there are bookshelves filled with books and a framed map on the wall. A white vertical bar with the number "2" is on the left side of the screen. The scene then transitions to a shot of several F-35 fighter jets slowly taxiing in a line on an asphalt runway, with trees in the background under a bright sky. This is followed by a view of a single F-35 jet taxiing towards the right, passing a line of parked F-15 fighter jets, with airport buildings and a communication tower visible in the background. The video then cuts back to the same man from the beginning, speaking and gesturing, now with a white vertical bar and the number "1" on the left, and the text "Scan Loss" appearing on the right side of the screen. The segment concludes with an animated graphic showing a white vertical bar with a small dish-like antenna and a dot, from which a line extends to the right towards a light blue, abstract background filled with glowing digital-like square patterns. The number "1" is still visible in the bottom left corner of this animation.

The video begins with an animation depicting a radar dish on the left, emitting a reddish-brown, elongated beam (representing the main lobe) along a central gray axis. A small black fighter jet initially appears on this axis. As the jet moves slightly off-axis, the beam attempts to track it, indicated by a dotted line. A graph below the animation illustrates the received signal intensity; initially, it's a strong, smooth red curve. As the jet moves further off-axis from the beam's center, the signal intensity depicted on the graph progressively decreases and becomes more jagged, demonstrating the concept of "scan loss." The video then transitions to a man with short dark hair and a beard, wearing a black jacket over a black t-shirt that reads "THE MAN MYTH THE LEGEND VINTAGE 1968 AGED PERFECTION." He stands in front of a wooden bookshelf filled with books and a framed map in the center. He holds a black tablet in his left hand and gestures with his right hand as he speaks. A white vertical bar with the number "1" is displayed on the left side of the screen. A speech bubble appears on the right with the text: "AESA radars may divide the scan volume in a few thousands fixed “points” and jump from point to point, not necessarily adjacent." Below the speech bubble, a small white circular device, resembling a modern radar antenna, is shown.

A man, wearing a black blazer over a black t-shirt with "THE MAN THE MYTH THE LEGEND VINTAGE 1968 AGED PERFECTLY ORIGINAL PARTS" printed on it, is seen in a room with bookshelves and a framed map behind him. He holds a black tablet in his left hand and gestures with his right hand as he explains a concept. On the right side of the screen, the text "Max deflection" appears. The video then transitions to a black silhouette of a fighter jet, which shoots out a light gray, cone-shaped beam from a blue rectangle at its nose. This transitions to a white background where lines emerge from the jet's nose, labeled "60° Max deflection" and "45° Sensitivity advantage", illustrating radar beam coverage that fades as deflection increases. The man reappears, continuing his explanation. The video then shows an overhead schematic of a fighter jet, possibly a Su-57, with multiple colored fan-shaped radar coverage areas (red, green, light blue) radiating from different parts of the aircraft. Greek text "Μποντα «X»" (Antenna "X"), "Μποντα «L»" (Antenna "L"), and "Μποντα «K»" (Antenna "K") labels some of these areas. The scene changes again to a gray Gripen fighter jet on display, with its nose cone open to reveal an orange radar dish rotating counter-clockwise, indicated by a yellow arrow. Finally, the video returns to the man, who concludes his segment by speaking and looking directly at the camera. A white vertical bar with the number "1" remains consistently on the left side of the screen throughout the video.

The video begins with a 3D animation showing numerous white cubes, each bearing the black text "CON". A glossy red sphere is positioned among them, initially showing indistinct text before rotating to display "PRO" in white letters. The scene then transitions to a man with short, dark hair and a beard, wearing a black blazer over a black t-shirt that reads "THE MAN THE LEGEND VINTAGE 1968 AGED TO PERFECTION ORIGINAL PART". He stands in a room with a large wooden bookshelf filled with books behind him, and a framed map or artwork on the wall between two sections of the shelf. He holds a black tablet or book in his left hand and gestures with his right hand as he speaks. As he asks, "Is it worth it?", the question appears as white text on the screen. He then opens his hands in a shrug, and a large white "YES!" overlay covers part of his body. He continues to speak, gesturing with his hands and pointing off-screen to his right. A PayPal logo and the text "https://www.paypal.me/millennium7star" appear at the bottom left of the screen. The video concludes with a black screen displaying a yellow and orange logo that reads "MILLENNIUM 7* MILITARY TECHNOLOGY EXPLAINED", followed by a disclaimer in white text: "No classified material was used in the making of this video and all the other videos in this channel and/or from the same author. The Author has no access to classified material of any nature. This video and all the other videos in this channel and/or from the same author are entirely based on public domain information. The appearance of U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) visual information does not imply or constitute DoD endorsement."
